title: The Concept of Dualism in Metaphysics
text:
Metaphysical dualism posits that reality fundamentally consists of two distinct and irreducible kinds of substances or properties. Historically, the most prominent formulation distinguishes between mind (or consciousness) and matter (or body). This viewpoint suggests that mental phenomena cannot be fully explained by purely physical laws, as thought seems to operate under non-material rules.

A major challenge posed by dualism is the problem of interaction: how exactly do two disparate substances—one non-physical and one physical—exchange energy or influence each other? If the mind is not material, it appears unable to exert force upon the brain, which operates purely within the realm of physics. Therefore, defining the mechanism of causal linkage between these two realms remains a deep philosophical hurdle.
